\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{সান্ত্বনা} (sāntvônā)}{সান্ত্বনা (sāntvônā)}]{\bn{সান্ত্বনা} (sāntvônā) — consolation; comfort}

\label{lesson:BN-C446-santvona}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to sob, then the Bengali for to lament.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{সান্ত্বনা}}
\textbf{\bn{সান্ত্বনা}} — \emph{sāntvônā} — \textquotedblleft{}consolation; comfort\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বন্ধুরা} \bn{এসে} \bn{মীরাকে} \bn{সান্ত্বনা} \bn{দিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bôndhurā ese mīrāke sāntvônā dilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Her friends came and consoled Mira.
\end{quote}

\bn{সান্ত্বনা} \bn{দেওয়া}, to console.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{সান্ত্বনা}} (\emph{sāntvônā}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{sāntvanā}, \textquotedblleft{}appeasing, soothing with kind words\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{স্বস্তি} (svôsti)}{স্বস্তি (svôsti)}]{\bn{স্বস্তি} (svôsti) — relief; ease of mind}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to lament, then the Bengali for consolation.
